messages:
Lena: Quick follow-up from Orchid postmortem. Summary: during an on‑prem maintenance the IPsec tunnel flapped and our peering-sync fell back to a permissive reconciliation path that inadvertently accepted a default-route advertisement from the edge appliance. Result: short-lived cross-tenant reachability.

Lena: Proposed actions: (A) harden peering-sync fallback logic to never accept default/0.0.0.0 routes from external peers (owner: Marcus, due 2026-04-08). (B) add a telemetry gate: if tunnel flap > 3 events in 15m, pause automated imports (owner: Zoe, due 2026-04-05). (C) run a monthly config-drift scan for onprem gateway ACL drift (owner: Priya, due 2026-04-12). (D) outreach draft for Orchid (owner: Lena, due 2026-03-31).

Marcus: I'll own A. Plan to add explicit default-route reject + unit tests and a canary flag. Will open PR and link to INC-23550.

Zoe: Taking B. I'll instrument the flap counter in the controller and add a circuit-breaker that triggers a read-only import-mode when exceeded. Will add e2e in the onprem harness.

Priya: I'll run the drift scan and produce a mitigation checklist for customers (ACL snapshot + expected baseline). Will surface any tenants with frequent gateway config changes.

eng-sre-bot: Created ticket INC-23550: "Orchid: peering-sync fallback hardening + drift scan" and assigned owners.

Lena: Short-term mitigation for Orchid: Marcus can flip a cluster-level strict-import toggle to block default routes; need ops to schedule a quick config push. Marcus: can you estimate time?

Marcus: Strict-toggle is small change, 30m to push + 15m validation per cluster. I'll coordinate with Dedicated ops.

Zoe: I'll add repro steps and a mini-scenario in the onprem lab so support can validate before any customer changes.

Priya: Audit kick-off now. Will post CSV of drifted customers to INC-23550 by EOD Thursday.

Lena: Thanks team. Please ack when you start and paste PR/ticket links here. We'll do a 15m sync Friday to confirm rollout windows.
